body:
I'd suggest getting rid of "Configures" outright for every affected tooltip. There's no rule for it. I just personally think it's strange to say in the same way it'd be, for example, when describing an Resource's property. These SpinBoxes represent the value as it is.
E.g. AudioStreamWAV's `mix_rate` doesn't *set*, rather it literally *is* the mix rate.

Another nitpick is that "tempo-synced looping" is a very unique way to word it that only really works because of the English language. It expands to "looping synced to the tempo", but even then I'm personally not sure if the meaning is clear enough.

```suggestion
	beats_edit->set_tooltip_text(TTR("The stream's length, in number of beats, used for tempo-synced looping and interactive streams.\nIf 0, it will be auto-detected from the stream's length.\nIt is recommended to set this value (either manually or by clicking on a beat number in the preview) to ensure looping works properly."));
```

I believe this is what it expands to?
```suggestion
	loop_offset->set_tooltip_text(TTR("The loop's offset, relative to the beginning of the stream. Represents the time in seconds at which the stream starts after looping."));
```

Do you have any suggestions? I don't believe "tempo-synced" and "beat-synced" are that much of unfamiliar terms, even for people new-ish to working with audio, and they're not too hard to figure out, I think. Also, "beat-sync" is a popular term in the area.
I have a preference for keeping "tempo-synced" and "beat-synced", but if you really think it doesn't work, I wouldn't mind changing to "looping synced to the tempo", or any other suggestion you may have. I could also try to get some thoughts from the audio team.

I'll happily apply the other suggested changes :)

It's a matter of taste, but I think this might be easier to understand

```suggestion
	loop_offset->set_tooltip_text(TTR("The loop start position, relative to the beginning of the stream, in seconds.\nThis is the position the playhead will return to when the end of the loop is reached."));
```

Nothing is really being "detected" here

```suggestion
	beats_edit->set_tooltip_text(TTR("The stream's length, in number of beats, used for tempo-synced looping and interactive streams.\nIf 0, the stream's duration will be used instead (rounded down to a whole number of beats).\nIt is recommended to set this value (either manually or by clicking on a beat number in the preview) to ensure looping works properly."));
```
I don't think I've seen "playhead" used anywhere else in the engine. Should we go with that or do you suggest a different word?

Playhead is a technical term i think. I can't say how many people would be familiar with it, but I'm guessing anyone in audio would know it, and I can't think of another term that describes the same thing

I get it, but I think "playhead" is a more visual term? It doesn't make much sense outside the stream importer with the preview. Any thoughts on "This is the position the stream's playback will return to when..." (more accurate), or more simply, "This is the position the stream will return to when..."?
Both of those work for me as well

Looking at the code again, I think the information it was trying to convey is just incorrect. If I'm not wrong, `beat_count` will remain 0 if not manually set. The mix function will just ignore it. In this case, I don't think "(rounded down to a whole number of beats)" is needed.
